text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers.
- German tyre maker Conti to halve production at its Austrian plant Semperit Reifen AG. More than a thousand jobs will be slashed, strike is planned.
- Retailer Spar plans to take over Magnet chain of ailing Loewa.
- Austrian tourism fell six percent in the summer.
- Austrian motorbike maker KTM has taken over the majority of its Swiss importer Fabag.

- Only 55 precent of Austrians have decided on who they will vote for in the October 13 elections for the European Parliament. Social-Democrats slightly ahead of Conservatives and the far-right Freedom party.
- Conservative People's party boss Wolfgang Schuessel says a referendum on neutrality is not necessary.
- Austrians claimed 14 sick days per capita, putting a heavy burden on the economy.
- No end to Austria's insolvencies in sight. In the first three quarters the number of insolvencies was up 9.6 percent to 1,656.
- Insurer Wiener Staedtische has taken over an 11.6 percent share of U.S. insurer Folksamerica.
- Doctors are still searching for the cause of President Klestil's pneumonia.
- Printer Leykam Medien AG plans to be listed on Vienna's stock exchange.
- Austria Tabak has to renegotiate contracts over its licences, European court rules.
- Austria has lost its competitive edge in the emerging markets, economic expert says.
